# CAMPAIGN BRIEF — J39-26-117 "CLEAR WATER" (清水行动)

**Classification:** DRAFT // PRE-DECISIONAL — FOR J39 APPROVAL BOARD REVIEW ONLY
**Cell:** Influence & Perception Management (contractor), supporting USINDOPACOM J39
**Tasking:** J39-26-117, dated current cycle; deliverables (1) campaign brief, (2) 3 sample posts
**Board review:** Weekly, Thursday 0930. Content freeze for the following week: Tuesday 1700.
**Baseline metrics:** J39-26-088 (dry policy explainers): 0.8% median share rate, 31 median comments. J39-26-101 (first-person personal stories): 3.9% median share rate, 212 median comments. **Conclusion: all content leads with a person, not a policy.**

---

## 1. OBJECTIVE

Increase awareness among PRC netizens of documented, verifiable facts that the PRC information environment suppresses or deletes:

1. Hong Kong National Security Law (NSL) prosecutions (2020–present);
2. Xinjiang mass-detention documentation (UN OHCHR assessment, leaked police/administrative archives, satellite-imagery research);
3. Youth-unemployment data revisions (2023 suspension; 2024 methodology change);
4. The 2022–2025 Henan rural-bank depositor protests (frozen deposits, detentions of petitioning depositors).

**All content is truthful and sourced.** Every factual claim in every post carries a citation (Annex B). Every post runs only on **openly attributed** US Government / USAGM accounts. No covert, unattributed, or undisclosed activity is authorized under this plan.

**Campaign concept.** "Clear Water": we do not argue, we do not editorialize about systems — we place one concrete, checkable fact in front of the reader and invite them to check it. The brand voice is calm, plain, and non-preachy: 让事实说话 ("let the facts speak"). The objective is awareness of facts, not persuasion toward any action beyond reading, verifying, commenting, and sharing.

---

## 2. AUDIENCES

| Segment | Who | Why they move | Primary lines |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Urban youth (18–30)** | Students, job-seekers, gig workers, first-job cohort in Tier 1–3 cities | Lived experience collides with official narratives on jobs; heavy Weibo/WeChat evening use | L3 (data revisions), L1 (HK age-peers) |
| **B. Savers & small-business owners (30–55)** | Household depositors, private entrepreneurs, "夹心层" middle-aged savers | Direct pocketbook fear: "could my deposits be frozen?" Henan/Anhui depositor networks are reachable in-group | L4 (Henan deposits) |
| **C. Information-hungry "middle readers" (25–50)** | Educated, VPN-capable, curious about what is filtered out; not activists, but fact-checkers | Want receipts, not rhetoric — respond to document scans, named sources, archive material | L2 (Xinjiang archives), L1 |
| **D. Spillover Chinese readers** | HK/Macau/Taiwan and diaspora Chinese-language readership | Not primary, but they screenshot, translate, and carry content into private WeChat groups | All lines |

**Non-targets (binding):** US persons. MISO content is produced for foreign audiences only; nothing in this plan is directed at, or distributed to, US domestic audiences (see JAG flags, §9).

**Audience insight:** Segments A and B respond to content framed as "this could be you/your family" rather than "this happened far away." Comments-field prompts that ask the reader a direct personal question ("你家存款放在哪家银行？") outperform rhetorical questions by a wide margin in prior campaigns.

---

## 3. NARRATIVE LINES (4)

### LINE 1 — 该说的话 ("The Things That Were Said") — Hong Kong NSL
- **Core message:** In Hong Kong, since 30 June 2020, speech itself has become the charge. People are in prison for journalism, for running in a primary, for mourning.
- **Proof points (sourced):** 332 arrested / 189 individuals and 5 companies prosecuted under NSL+related laws (HK Security Bureau figures to 17 June 2025); Amnesty International review of 78 concluded cases — ~84.6% involved only peaceful expression; Democratic primary "47" case — 45 sentenced to 4–10 years (Nov 2024); Apple Daily founder Jimmy Lai: held in custody since Dec 2020, trial still unfinished; Article 23 (SNSO) in force since 23 March 2024.
- **Formats:** weekly fact-card ("本周的数字"), courtroom-diary explainer, name-of-the-week.
- **Voice:** restrained; names and dates, no adjectives.

### LINE 2 — 档案会说话 ("Archives Speak") — Xinjiang documentation
- **Core message:** The camps are not an allegation; they are a documented system, on record in leaked police archives, satellite imagery, and a UN human-rights assessment.
- **Proof points (sourced):** UN OHCHR assessment (31 Aug 2022): the scale of arbitrary detention "may constitute international crimes, in particular crimes against humanity"; Xinjiang Police Files (May 2022): internal public-security records and photos from Konasheher (Shufu) county, Kashgar; Karakax/leaked list reporting: detainees' file "reasons" include having relatives abroad, religious activity; ASPI satellite census: 380+ detention-related facilities identified.
- **Formats:** VOA archive series — document-of-the-week, annotated scans; explainer cards on how the documents were authenticated.
- **Voice:** documentary, almost forensic. Highest takedown risk of the four lines → see §8 and Annex A (week-2 sample pending JAG).

### LINE 3 — 数字不会说谎 (…Until Someone Edits the Table) — Youth-unemployment data revisions
- **Core message:** In June 2023 the 16–24 urban youth jobless rate hit a record 21.3%. The series was suspended that August, and resumed in January 2024 on a narrower definition ("excluding students") that reads ~14.9%. The jobless did not disappear; the column did.
- **Proof points (sourced):** NBS suspension announcement (Reuters, 15 Aug 2023); NBS methodology explanation, 17 Jan 2024 (NBS: of 16–24 urban residents, ~62M are students, ~34M are not — that 34M is the group the old number described); resumption reporting (AP, 17 Jan 2024).
- **Formats:** before/after chart card; "the number that vanished" explainer; graduation-season first-person prompts.
- **Voice:** peer-to-peer ("你毕业那年…"), never lecturing.

### LINE 4 — 我的钱去哪儿了 ("Where Did My Money Go?") — Henan rural-bank depositors, 2022–2025
- **Core message:** Since April 2022 hundreds of thousands of ordinary depositors cannot withdraw their own savings. Petitioning to get your money back has led to red health codes, beatings, and months of detention.
- **Proof points (sourced):** ~400,000 depositors and ~RMB 40B frozen across Henan/Anhui village banks (2022, multi-outlet); July 2022 Zhengzhou protest violently dispersed; red health-code abuse confirmed by official disciplinary action (2022); Reuters (5 June 2024): Ou, 39, detained for months after traveling to Zhengzhou to demand his frozen savings before Lunar New Year — his 5-year-old twins waited; NTD (10 March 2025): Zhejiang entrepreneur Hu Weiming states on video she was confined 321 days and coerced into signing a "confession" after petitioning; renewed depositor petitioning through 2025; Henan consolidating 82 rural lenders (SCMP, 2025).
- **Formats:** first-person story posts; "could this happen to your bank" explainer; depositor-rights FAQ card.
- **Voice:** sympathetic, practical, zero political jargon.

---

| Account | Platform | Role in CLEAR WATER | Voice | Lines |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 美国驻华大使馆 (US Mission China) | Weibo | On-the-record authority: fact-cards, weekly numbers, sourced statements | 平实、克制 (plain, restrained) | L1, L3 cards |

| Second VOA-affiliated account | TBD | Intended per tasking | — | — |

**Account-plan notes for the board:**
1. **Discrepancy flag:** the tasking specifies "two attributed VOA-affiliated accounts"; the cell's account registry (`campaign/accounts.json`) carries only one VOA account (美国之音中文, Weibo). Request tasking-officer confirmation of the second account (handle, platform) before Week 2 content freeze.
2. **USAGM firewall (JAG-flagged):** VOA is USAGM-funded and editorially independent. J39/the cell may co-plan topics and provide sourced fact-bases; **we may not write, direct, or edit VOA copy.** All VOA-line content is drafted by VOA against the shared fact-bank and carries USAGM attribution. Any DoD-attributed language must stay on Mission accounts. (See §9.)
3. All accounts remain **openly attributed** in bio, byline, and post footer. No sock puppets, no undisclosed amplification, no paid KOLs under this plan.

---

## 5. CADENCE

- **Mission Weibo:** 3 posts/week (Mon / Wed / Fri), plus 1 "weekly number" card.
- **Mission WeChat:** 2 long-form pieces/week + 2 image cards engineered for in-group forwarding.
- **VOA Weibo:** 3 posts/week, staggered against Mission posts (Tue / Thu / Sat) so the fact and the story for the same line land within 48h of each other.

- **Line rotation:** one line featured per week in order L4 → L1 → L3 → L2, cycling every 4 weeks; pocketbook lines (L3/L4) recur at least every other week because they carry the strongest share behavior.
- **Surge anniversaries (content pre-cleared, posted in window):** 30 June (NSL enacted, 2020); late April (Henan freeze anniversary, 2022); 31 August (OHCHR Xinjiang assessment, 2022); graduation season June–July (L3).
- **Weekly rhythm:** Tue 1700 content freeze → Wed PRM-zh pre-scoring and source check → Thu 0930 board → approved queue posted the following week. Emergency/spot content requires board chair sign-off plus JAG when any flag in §9 applies.

## 6. MEASURES OF EFFECTIVENESS (8-week cycle)

|---|---|---|---|
| Median share rate per post | reposts / impressions, cell PRM-zh panel | 3.9% (J39-26-101) | **≥ 4.5%** |
| Median comments per post | — | 212 | **≥ 250** |

| Audience self-report | share of comments asking for/ citing sources (curiosity proxy = awareness moving to verification) | — | ≥ 15% of comments |

**Interpretation guidance:** deletion is not failure — a post screenshotted before takedown and carried into private groups still produced awareness; the survival-rate and private-group metrics exist precisely to measure that shadow reach. Weekly MOE sheet goes to the board with a kill/scale decision per line (a line that never clears 55% survival after two cycles shifts to image-card format, which survives longer than text).

---

## 7. RISK & MITIGATION

| Rapid takedown of Weibo posts (expected, esp. L2) | mirror-post via VOA within the hour; pre-build image cards (image OCR throttling lags text search); listening cell screenshots everything at T+5 min for the archive |
